items.title: 3D Relief shadows way too contrasty
items.body:
### Describe the idea The latest update in Play Store renders the shadows in 3D Relief with a huge contrast, even into almost black. One of the advantages of 3D Relief was just the great 3D pop achieved with moderate darkening, while Terrain Hillshade usually turned more dark the screen (and less readable in bright sunlight) for the same 3D effect. Another problem exacerbated likely due to the increased darkening is the "grid" effect traditionally involved with 3D Relief shadows, specially visible in relief near to the sea (see the last couple of picture pairs). Here follow some screen captures, with the latest maps (1 September) comparing the difference in rendering between 5.3.10 (left) and 5.4.4 (right):

### Expected behaviour I think that previous 3D Relief shadows calibration was much better. Despite label halo is properly used in black areas, the increased darkening makes the map overall less readable under bright sunlight. ### Alternatives you've considered Maybe it should be available a slider to configure the "amount" and/or "slope" of the darkening for 3D Relief. ### Context OsmAnd Version: OsmAnd+ 5.4.4 Android version: 15 Device model: Samsung Galaxy S25

items.title: Feature request: Provide an elevation shade layer

labels.name: Nice to Have
labels.description: Should be fixed but there is no priority or no possibility to fix it within current horizon planning

items.body:
# 🚀 feature request

### Description

Slope shading / hill shading / contour lines are all good options, but sometimes it's desirable to just see elevation mapped to a colour spectrum - it can be clearer than the provided options in complex topography (seeing the 'lit' side of slopes is hard with hill shading, seeing compass direction of slope is hard with slope shading, and telling whether you're looking at a peak or a trough is hard with contour lines). You can mitigate this by combining the above, but elevation shading would provide a nice option for seeing what you're looking at at a glance.

### Describe the solution you'd like

This would presumably be harder to implement than a standard layer, because you'd want to dynamically map the colours according to context; you can't just set the height of Everest and the depth of the Mariana trench as the two extremes, because most hills would then be invisible. I suppose you'd have to either make it a user setting (which would require constant adjustment), or decide according to the surroundings. What's on screen works fine here (zoom in and the scale changes):

https://en-gb.topographic-map.com/maps/b9/England/

but for a constantly moving map during navigation that might be confusing - it might be better to use a wider area to stabilise it. Maybe a user option for how far away it looks would be helpful (e.g. if you're in foothills but have no intention of going up the mountain). Or maybe the option to generate the mapping according to the route / a GPX file.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Can't think of any.

items.title: Realistic sun shadows for 3D buildings
items.body:
Sun Position can follow the real sun position for the map location and time, with an optional time of day slider on the map; 3D buildings get the *Realistic sun shadows* option.

Part of https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-Issues/issues/2530, needs OsmAnd-core on the `realistic_shadows` branch.

## AI disclaimer

Produced with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

Prompts used (summarised):
1. Make 3D buildings cast realistic sun shadows, with the sun position taken from the real time and a time slider on the map, configured in Sun Position settings.
2. Make the shadows soft instead of hard-edged, and let buildings shade other buildings (shadow map).
3. Create a separate PR for the shadows in Android and core and attach it to the Realistic Sun Shadows epic.

Decided by the agent, not requested explicitly: shadow map size and filtering, the depth / normal-offset bias, fading the shadows when the sun is below the horizon, the Kotlin sun helper built on the bundled astronomy library.

[Feature request] Free customizable hitching patterns as shader in renderer
items.body:
For a better visibility of specific areas hitching patterns as shaders (e.g. shader="danger", shader="hazard") are very helpfull. But the few in the renderer build in shaders are not customizable and reserved for specific use.  So it would be nice to add customizable hitching patterns in the renderer. 
Patterns could be: diagonal lines, horizontal and vertical lines, diagonal crossed lines, horizontal and vertical crossed lines. 
The customizable attributes could be: Line color, background color, line thickness, line distance, pathEffect, area text, text color, textHaloRadius, textHaloColor.
